subtitle: Search me before you fix them.
note: Six reels and three carousels, Mon 5 to Sat 10 Oct, built on one line: Search me before you fix them. Each reel: OpusClip clip (emojis off) + a three-card closing designed in ChatGPT and animated here + an end card, voice lifted to -14 LUFS with a hymn bed at -6dB. Excluded on care grounds: the clips retelling the Bathsheba and Uriah story in detail, and the judgement clip without the turn to grace. The recorded cut ends mid point 3, so the Rich Young Ruler, Isaiah 6 and the conclusion are not in this pack.
voice_note: Quote marks only for his verified spoken words. Trials "expose" what is there; copy avoids both "weaknesses" and "wickedness".

posts.title: God Sees the Why
posts.endline: It's easy to look right on the outside. → The real question is what's driving it. → for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart. (1 Samuel 16:7)

captions.instagram:
People can see what you do. Only God sees why you do it.

You can serve, give, show up and say all the right things, and still be driven by pride, envy or the need to be noticed. Pastor Kayode puts it simply: God is not just concerned about what we do, He is concerned about why we do it.

God already knows what is in our hearts. The invitation is for us to become honest enough to let Him show us too.

Search me, O God, and know my heart. Psalm 139:23

Watch the full message by searching Calvary Hephzibah on YouTube.

posts.title: Search Me Before You Fix Them

captions.instagram:
Search me before you fix them.

It is easy to see what is wrong with everyone else, and even easier to pray about it. Fix their attitude. Change their decisions. Deal with their pride.

David prayed differently. Search me, O God, and know my heart. Psalm 139:23

This week, before you pray about the people around you, ask God to show you what He sees in you. Start with your own heart. Then pray for theirs.

posts.title: That Is You
posts.endline: Nathan told King David a story about someone else. → It's easy to judge the problem until it has your name on it. → And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. (2 Samuel 12:7)

captions.instagram:
It's easy to see the problem when it's someone else's story.

Nathan told King David about a rich man who took a poor man's only lamb. David was outraged and said that man should be punished. Then Nathan turned the story around. Thou art the man. 2 Samuel 12:7

Pastor Kayode reminds us that we often see clearly in other people what we cannot see in ourselves.

What would God show you if you let Him tell the story back to you?

posts.title: He Just Owned Up
posts.quote: I have sinned against the Lord.
posts.endline: No excuses. No blame. → He owned the truth. God met him with grace. → Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me. (Psalm 51:10)

captions.instagram:
When David was confronted, he did not argue, explain or point at anyone else.

Pastor Kayode puts it plainly: he didn't make any excuses, he just owned up. I have sinned against the Lord. And the answer came straight back: the Lord has taken away your sin.

Honesty with God is not the end of the story. It is where grace meets us.

Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me. Psalm 51:10

Watch the full message by searching Calvary Hephzibah on YouTube.

posts.title: Why Is It Easier to See It in Them?

captions.instagram:
Why is it easier to see it in them than in me?

We notice someone else's temper, pride or excuses straight away, and somehow miss the same things in ourselves. Even David couldn't see it until Nathan told him the story.

So before you point, pause. Ask God to show you what you can't see. Then try three honest questions:

What frustrates me most in others?
Where might that be true of me?
Who could be honest with me?

Why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Matthew 7:3

Watch the full message, Search Me, O GOD, by searching Calvary Hephzibah on YouTube.

posts.title: What Tests Reveal
posts.endline: It's easy to be patient when nobody's pushing. → Pressure doesn't hide what's there. It brings it to the surface. → Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts. (Psalm 139:23)

captions.instagram:
You don't really know how patient you are until someone pushes you.

Pastor Kayode put it this way: you may think you're patient until you face provocation. You may think you trust God until you meet uncertainty. You may think you're humble until you're overlooked.

Tests don't put something new in us. They show what was already there. And that is a gift, because what God shows us, He can change.

Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts. Psalm 139:23

Watch the full message by searching Calvary Hephzibah on YouTube.

posts.title: Failure Isn't the End
posts.endline: Peter said he'd never deny Jesus. He did. Three times. → But his worst moment wasn't his last. → But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not. (Luke 22:32)

captions.instagram:
Peter was bold. He told Jesus that even if everyone else walked away, he never would.

Then a servant girl asked if he knew Him. He denied it. Three times.

Pastor Kayode says the test showed Peter something he didn't know about himself: his self-confidence was stronger than his dependence on God.

But that failure was not the end of Peter. It became the beginning of his transformation. The broken Peter became the powerful Peter of Pentecost.

If you're carrying a failure today, it doesn't have to be your last word either.

But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not. Luke 22:32

Watch the full message by searching Calvary Hephzibah on YouTube.

posts.title: You Don't Really Know Until It's Tested

captions.instagram:
You don't really know until it's tested.

You may think you're patient until someone provokes you. You may think you trust God until things get uncertain. You may think you're humble until you're overlooked.

Pastor Kayode's point is simple: tests don't create what's in us. They reveal it. That isn't bad news. You can't grow in what you can't see.

Next time you're tested, don't only ask for it to end. Ask what it's showing you.

Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. James 1:3

Watch the full message, Search Me, O GOD, by searching Calvary Hephzibah on YouTube.

Which of the three tests you most? 👇

posts.title: What Are You Teaching Me?
posts.quote: Lord, show me what You are teaching me through this challenge.
posts.endline: We pray for the challenge to go away. → Sometimes the better prayer is What are You teaching me? → And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting. (Psalm 139:24)

captions.instagram:
We pray for the challenge to go away.

Take it away. Fix it. Move it out of my way.

Pastor Kayode suggests a different prayer for the hard seasons: "Lord, show me what You are teaching me through this challenge."

It may be, he says, that God wants us to learn something from that challenge, and that is why it is in our way.

So before you ask for it to be gone, ask what it is showing you.

And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting. Psalm 139:24
